source: And I don't think we can continue this liaison any longer.
Ah. I see. How inappropriate of me. Of course... we... mustn't.
You're right. It was all moving terribly fast. I see that now.
I have intruded long enough.
Please leave me be. I need to be alone now.
I thought you'd gone.
If you'd like to return to your chambers, you're free to go, of course.
Ophelia. Follow me. There's something I'd like to show you.
Please, be seated.
On the Queen's...?
I cannot bear to let it sit empty. And it isn't right that it should remain so.
She would have wanted you to sit there, I think.
This is strange.
Yet, somehow—natural.
As I said before: you would make a fine Queen.
And, as well as I could have hoped, peace has at last come to Denmark.
Is that... would being my wife... be... amenable... to you?
The betrothal would be long. As long as one might be. To give the both of us time.
(This is moving so quickly...)
(Then again, I have only... a little time remaining. Perhaps it would be worthwhile to follow this path to its end.)
Accept Claudius's offer of a betrothal?

source: I have... never found a place for myself within Elsinore.
Perhaps it was because my fate lay here, on the throne.
The marriage must be approved. You are, of course, of sufficient rank, but they may question your mother's lineage.
I won't let that stand in the way, though.
My dear, there's going to be a wonderful end to this terrible summer after all.
I can't accept this, Claudius. I'm sorry.
I... it would be... too much. Too soon.
Maybe the Queen would have wanted this, but maybe she wouldn't.
She's been dead just a short time. It... feels wrong.
Yes, I see. Of course I do.
Please... excuse me. I have merely awoken from a short and horrible dream.
Apologies, ladies and gentlemen, for disturbing you.
There have been some... troubling circumstances. The castle is in a state of emergency until my men and I are able to investigate thoroughly.
Lord Polonius died very suddenly last night as part of a deeply unfortunate accident. He died at the Prince's hand.
That boy.
My men and I are still uncovering information about the event itself. I ask for your compassion for Lady Ophelia and Lord Laertes in this horrific time.
Lord Polonius served the castle faithfully all his life.
Whatever particulars surround his death, let us remember him as he was: a stalwart advisor to His Majesty Claudius, and to King Hamlet before him.
Ophelia. I'm so sorry. This is rotten. All of this.
Is there anything I can do for you? Anything you need?
No. Just send word to my brother, please.
It still hardly feels real, Horatio.
Be kind to yourself today. Give it time.
I'm so sorry to hear about your father's passing. No one should have to witness such a thing.
I'm sorry to be the one to tell you this.
Your father is dead.
There was an... altercation with the Prince.
There was an... altercation with the Queen.
There was an... incident involving His Majesty.
In the King's chambers?
Yes. How did you know?
Call it an inkling.
What? But I thought Father was--
(I thought I saved him.)
What happened? Where was he?
All I know is that your father was in the King's chambers with him, alone.
Then one of the guards was called in, only to find your father had collapsed.
The King claims he fainted suddenly. It's possible it was a natural death.
Possible? This is Claudius we're talking about.
I have no means to know for certain. I was not present for your father's passing.
And without that knowledge, I must take the King's word on faith about what occurred.
He took his own life rather suddenly.
I know it's not easy to hear it this way. I'm sorry to cause you shock.
(His death was by my hand this time. Even though it's temporary, it still hurts.)
My lady, if there's anything I can do...
No, Bernardo. That's quite all right. I'll see him again soon enough.
I can only hope so. May we all be reunited in Heaven.
Heaven. Of course.
But I am searching for answers with all my power right now. I wanted to assure you of that.
I couldn't save him this time, after all.
No one would dare believe this was your fault, Ophelia. Please don't blame yourself.
No. You're wrong.
I will save him. I have to.
S-save him? Er...
My lady, please... Get some rest tonight. We'll speak soon.
He was a good man. A great man.
I can only hope so. May we all be reunited in the afterlife.
Yes. The afterlife. Of course.
It's difficult to process, I'm sorry. I should leave you be.
Your brother has already been informed. You should go to him.
My father... there was something he wanted me to have. A key to the chest in his room.
Ah, yes. We did find something like that.
It's yours now. The least I can do, my lady.
I'm truly sorry, Ophelia. But... now I must inform the rest of the castle.
...That's the herald's horn.
Something's happened.
Listen to the announcement?

source: I have an important update regarding the alleged spy in our midst.
The King has passed.
As a result, no festivals or celebration will be observed for some days. His loss is keenly felt by us all, I'm certain.
It was a horrible accident. I ask all of you to give Her Majesty space to heal and grieve at this time.
It appears Her Majesty raised a weapon against him. I'm still trying to understand why this took place.
His Majesty and the Prince... well, I'll leave it to His Highness to describe what transpired between them.
Needless to say, it was a tragic accident. We shall all mourn him deeply.
His Majesty and the Prince... well. Needless to say, it was a tragic accident. We shall all mourn him deeply.
He was murdered by an unknown assailant. We have no context at this time.
Still, I believe there is little immediate threat of danger to the rest of us. I'll announce information as I obtain it.
As most of you have no doubt heard by now, the King and Queen became suddenly ill in the middle of their meal, and perished shortly afterwards.
We confirmed that Irma had poisoned them both. She confessed immediately, and has been imprisoned and formally sentenced for her crime.
May God rest their souls.
We're still attempting to get to the bottom of what happened.
This is 'orrible. I canna' believe it.
(He's really dead.)
Good riddance, I say.
H-his majesty?
The nobility will soon meet to arrange a vote. In the interim, by our custom, Hamlet would traditionally carry on the duties his uncle leaves behind.
My lord, are you prepared for that?
I-- if that's what I must do.
I need-- some time to think about it.
But I think my own father would have wanted this of me. For me to take the throne.
You don't have to do this, my Prince.
Please. Just give me time.
Of course. As you wish.
Unfortunately, with Hamlet's passing, there is no immediate successor to the throne.
The noblemen of Denmark will convene within a week to determine the best path forward.
This is a dark moment for us all.
And the Queen's death was, truly, entirely unexpected.
The Queen's death was entirely unexpected.
That my lady's closest confidante would do this to her is nearly unthinkable.
We found her at the foot of the eastern wall this morning, on the beach.
We're not sure what occurred, or whether she was alone at the moment she died.
She appears to have suddenly lost her life during a confrontation with the Prince.
N-no... Gerta...
T-truly? How awful.
(He looks pale. Paler than I've ever seen him. I wonder if he'll be all right.)
Some of you know that Hamlet has also departed us far too soon.
Some of you know that Hamlet has departed us far too soon.
He lost a duel against the king.
The Queen has not been located as of yet, but we hope to do so soon.
His body was found at the foot of the walls. He was--
I hope to never see the like of that scene again.
A most unfortunate accident.
Lady Brit found him alone in his chambers. His assailant is unknown.
His body was found alongside his mother's.
Our best guess is that he became hostile, and with no one else around, she was forced to defend herself.
(If I had stayed...)
Hamlet was a lifelong friend of mine. I will miss him from the deepest part of my heart.
H-Hamlet. This... feels... unreal.
With both the King and the Prince having passed, we are left without a clear direction to proceed.
I'm afraid the throne will remain vacant until the nobles can reconvene.
I also must regret to inform you all that Lord Polonius has passed away.
There was an incident with Prince Hamlet. The situation escalated.
Although neither can be faulted for the outcome, this tragic accident cost Lord Polonius his life.
Hamlet's soul must surely be beyond saving now.
Not to mention that Laertes, who passed away suddenly, must be put to rest as soon as possible.
(...I'm so sorry, Laertes.)
Even during these tragedies, I have carried out my duty. The traitor Birgitta has been put to death.
The traitor Birgitta has been put to death.
Let this serve as a warning for all that would betray the Crown.
So be it, then.
I apologize, everyone, for the disturbance. But sudden death like this always warrants a heightened awareness.
I encourage all of you to report anything troubling you see to me at once. And remain within the castle, if possible.
No, I'd rather be alone right now.
Not now. I'm busy.
So terribly good to see you once again.
Especially after what transpired last time.
You. Do you...
...Do I remember you?
Thank goodness. I'm not going insane.
Time is repeating, somehow. Everything's so strange. First that horrible dream, and now this.
Your father's death, and then your own. Surely the vision you had showed you such a fate.
How do you know these things?
Did you cause them to happen? Are you some sort of-- sorcerer?
No, I didn't. I mean you no harm, Lady Ophelia. I merely aim to offer my assistance in your journey.
Just as I did for His Majesty King Hamlet, once.
Is my vision a portent of the future? Will my father's murder continue to come to pass?
A-and-- someone's coming to kill me too, aren't they?
Who can save us? Who can protect us?
Who indeed, Lady Ophelia?
Unfortunately, this is a road which must be traveled alone. And it is a lonely one, indeed.
